messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Alternatively, the dosage is 80 mL of the 5 mg/mL oral solution.
Extended-release tramadol has a lower daily limit of 300 mg, taken as one dose once a day.
Always check the strength printed on your own bottle or packet.
Do not take tramadol together with any other medicine that contains tramadol.
If you miss a dose, take your next dose at your usual time.
Swallow the capsule or tablet whole to avoid exposure to a potentially fatal overdose.
Do not crush, chew, break, open, or dissolve.
Never crush or break a tramadol tablet to inhale the powder or mix tramadol tablet into a liquid to inject tramadol into your vein.
This practice has resulted in death.
May be taken with or without food.
If you take the oral solution:
Tramadol oral solution is measured in millilitres (mL), not milligrams (mg).
It contains 5 mg of tramadol in every 1 mL.
Confusing the two units can cause a fatal overdose.
Always measure your dose with a graduated oral syringe or measuring cup marked in mL.
Your pharmacy can supply these tools.
Never measure your dose with a household teaspoon or tablespoon.
Triples: [["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "dosage is 80 mL of the 5 mg/mL oral solution"], ["extended-release tramadol", "has daily dose limit", "300 mg"], ["extended-release tramadol", "has administration instruction", "taken as one dose once a day"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "always check the strength printed on your own bottle or packet"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "do not take tramadol together with any other medicine that contains tramadol"], ["tramadol", "has missed dose instruction", "take your next dose at your usual time"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "swallow the capsule or tablet whole to avoid exposure to a potentially fatal overdose"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "do not crush, chew, break, open, or dissolve"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "never crush or break a tramadol tablet to inhale the powder or mix tramadol tablet into a liquid to inject tramadol into your vein"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "this practice has resulted in death"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "may be taken with or without food"], ["tramadol oral solution", "measured in", "millilitres (mL)"], ["tramadol oral solution", "not measured in", "milligrams (mg)"], ["tramadol oral solution", "contains", "5 mg of tramadol in every 1 mL"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "confusing the two units can cause a fatal overdose"], ["tramadol oral solution", "has administration instruction", "always measure your dose with a graduated oral syringe or measuring cup marked in mL"], ["tramadol oral solution", "has administration instruction", "your pharmacy can supply these tools"], ["tramadol oral solution", "has administration instruction", "never measure your dose with a household teaspoon or tablespoon"]]
Relations: ["contains", "has administration instruction", "has daily dose limit", "has missed dose instruction", "measured in", "not measured in"]
Answer:

completion:
contains: The subject entity includes or comprises the substance or component specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject entity should be administered according to the specific instruction provided by the object entity.  
has daily dose limit: The subject entity has a maximum daily dose specified by the object entity.  
has missed dose instruction: The subject entity has specific instructions for what to do if a dose is missed, as specified by the object entity.  
measured in: The subject entity is quantified or measured using the unit specified by the object entity.  
not measured in: The subject entity is not quantified or measured using the unit specified by the object entity.
